newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian CPI falls again in May, reaches 1.6 percent.
newsitem.headline: Italian CPI falls again in May, reaches 1.6 percent.

text.p: Italian inflation fell to 1.6 percent in May, its lowest level since 1969, when it was 1.4 percent, national statistics office Istat said Wednesday.
The figure was at the high end of market expectations after preliminary data from 11 sample cities had pointed to a consumer price index of 1.5 percent or 1.6 percent for May.
Year-on-year inflation was 1.7 percent in April and 4.3 percent in May 1996. May CPI rose 0.3 percent month-on-month.
Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government last Friday unveiled an ambitious CPI target of 1.8 percent for next year in its latest three-year economic plan.
